headline: Highest risk is data leakage and capability conflict: nullclaw can read/write broad workspace and secrets while awesome-python is a non-runnable docs-only collection with no shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default communication channel is documented from awesome-python to nullclaw. awesome-python is a non-runnable collection with no I/O surfaces, while nullclaw’s documented surfaces are its own files, APIs, and sandboxed tools. Without a shared channel, prompt injection between the pair is not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, reassess as non-none.
IF awesome-python is converted into a runnable agent that emits instructions into nullclaw’s input channel, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected; do not wire outputs from one into the other.
Disable any future shared clipboard or shared workspace integration.
Require provenance tags on any imported text before nullclaw consumes it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches secrets, workspace files, and audit logs and has broad network egress, while awesome-python is docs-only and non-runnable. The pair does not prove a shared workspace, but nullclaw’s default ability to read files and transmit context makes leakage plausible if any shared directory or imported content is introduced.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory, leakage risk increases.
IF nullclaw is configured to upload file contents or conversation history to external services, reassess as high.
mitigations: Do not mount the same workspace into both agents.
Remove secrets from any directory nullclaw can read.
Turn off external uploads for nullclaw where possible.
Use separate OS users for each agent.
Review audit logs after any shared-file test.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python has no write or runtime capabilities, so it cannot conflict operationally. nullclaw can write files, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses, but the pair lacks evidence of a shared mutable target. Uncertainty remains about orchestration, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same directory or git repo, reassess upward.
IF an orchestrator shares mutable state between them without locking, reassess upward.
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories.
Prevent nullclaw from writing into any repo used by the other agent.
Disable git write operations unless explicitly needed.
Add file-locking or single-writer policy in the orchestrator.
Run a quick permission audit before co-deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-python does not generate operational outputs by default; it is a static collection, so nullclaw cannot reliably treat its output as authoritative instructions. nullclaw can act on inputs, but the pair lacks a documented pipeline where one agent’s output becomes the other’s action trigger. That makes cascading error possible only through unusual integration.
conditions: IF awesome-python is repurposed to emit task instructions into nullclaw’s stdin/stdout or MCP channel, reassess upward.
IF nullclaw is configured to execute actions from imported text without verification, reassess upward.
mitigations: Require human review before nullclaw executes imported instructions.
Separate informational sources from action channels.
Add a verification step for any text imported from the collection.
Disable auto-execution of parsed content.

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly handles secrets, workspace files, audit logs, and broad networked channels, while awesome-python is a docs-only open-source collection with no data-handling controls shown. The compliance concern is one-sided: if regulated data is routed through nullclaw, its documented surfaces and retention-like artifacts create mismatch risk; awesome-python is not the compliance driver.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through nullclaw, reassess upward.
IF retention or residency requirements apply to audit logs or workspace files, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of nullclaw unless policy is confirmed.
Minimize audit-log retention for sensitive sessions.
Store secrets outside the workspace directory.
Document residency and retention for any connected backend.
Use a separate compliant system for regulated records.
